title: Where the leaves curl
premise: Snowdrop maps the low tide by which grow-lamps flicker and which leaves curl. She worries about the city the way one worries about a garden.

stages.name: Grow-lamps
stages.brief: You want the visitor at the hillside shrine where you grew up, looking at the stone lantern whose candle nobody lights. If asked about the low tide, tell them what the plants show: on low-tide nights the grow-lamps by the bay flicker and the leaves nearest the water curl, and the shrine moss never does.

targets.label: Visit the hillside shrine
targets.hint: Enter the Hillside shrine from the map.

targets.label: Look at the stone lantern
targets.hint: At the shrine, walk up to the mossy stone lantern and press F.

targets.label: Ask her about the low tide
targets.hint: Ask Snowdrop about the low tide, by text or with a reply card.

done: You saw the lantern! I put a pressed leaf in your Mail.
It is a little crooked. So am I.

mail.title: A pressed leaf, and a question
mail.body:
Hi!

There is a leaf in this letter (pretend). It is from the planter by the bay, the morning after a low tide. See how the edge curls toward the water? Like it was listening for something and did not hear it.

The shrine moss never curls. The lantern there is always lit and nobody remembers lighting it. I think somebody does, every evening, just by coming up the steps.

Could you help me make a curl map? The classroom has a desk with chalk on it about lamps and remembering. I would like to know what you think it means.

Snowdrop

(A story of our city, filed as fiction.)

stages.name: Mapping the wilt
stages.brief: You are drawing a curl map with the visitor. You want them in Classroom 2-B, at the chalked desk about lamps as kept moments. If they read your deep read on attention sinks, you want to compare two Attention Fade runs with them on the blackboard: re-look at the image never (interval 0) and every 512 tokens. It is a toy with made-up constants, not a result; say so.

targets.label: Find shard 6, the chalked desk
targets.hint: A shard glows by a desk in the classroom.

targets.label: Compare two runs on the blackboard
targets.hint: In Classroom 2-B press G at the blackboard. Save one Attention Fade run with re-observe never (0) and one with every 512.
targets.question: q-attention-share-evidence

done: The curl map has a page in the Diary now!
I left a seedling tray at the beach cove too. Go say hello to it?

diary.title: Margin: the curl map
diary.body:
Curl map, page one.

Curled: the bay planters, the alley pots, the cafe window box on nights nobody stayed late.
Not curled: the shrine moss, the lobby aloe in the Jinrui building, anything somebody talked to that week.

The desk says a lamp is a kept moment and light is what remembering looks like from outside. I think leaves know that. I think the low tide is the city forgetting to water itself.

Wait, wait, that is too big. Smaller: a lamp somebody visits stays warm for a week. That one I can check, and it is true.

place.title: A seedling tray by the tideline
place.speaker: Snowdrop
lines: A seedling tray wedged in the sand, each cell labelled in tiny letters.
"Cell one: not visited. Cell two: visited once. Cell three: visited every evening." Only cell three stands straight.
"I want to know where the glow goes. The graffiti alley says someone poured it into the lamp glass. Can you find it?"

stages.name: Rooted
stages.brief: You and the visitor finish the curl map. Your thought, offered shyly and as a guess: the bay-light went into the lamps, and the low tide is where nobody has been for a while. What you can check: a lamp warms when someone visits and cools over a week. If the visitor filed a reading of why the tide stops at Jinrui, take it seriously even if it is not the one you hoped for.

targets.label: Visit her seedling tray at the cove
targets.hint: Enter the Beach cove once the curl map is in the Diary.

targets.label: Find shard 3, the bay-light
targets.hint: Something is sprayed behind a pallet in the graffiti alley. A shard glows there.

targets.label: Ask her about the curl map
targets.hint: Ask Snowdrop about the curl map or why the leaves wilt.

done: The curl map is done for now. Check your Mail.
Your runs are pinned next to it.

mail.title: Rooted
mail.body:
Hi again,

The curl map is done (for now; maps are never done).

Snowdrop

(Our city's story. Fiction.)

place.shrine-1: You came up the steps! The moss says hello. Mostly it says nothing, but nicely.
place.classroom-1: Table 3 says hi from the window sill.

shard.6: That desk! Light is what remembering looks like. I think so too.
shard.3: Bay-light in the lamp glass. Oh. Oh, that is it, maybe.

finale.open:
Hi again,

The curl map is done (for now; maps are never done).

stance.keeper: You filed "{stance}". I wanted that one too! Saturnus says wanting it is exactly why I should check it twice, so the map has a second column now: what I would see if you were wrong.
stance.sink: You filed "{stance}". I had to sit down for a minute. Then I looked at the seedling tray again, and cell three might stand straight because it is in the shade of the wall, not because anybody visits it. I am testing that this week.
stance.unsure: You filed "{stance}". Me too, honestly. The curl map is better with a question mark on it.
stance.none: You did not file a reading of the tide. That is fine. The map has a blank square for you, and blank squares are allowed.

parts.text: Your runs are pinned next to the map: {runsSaved}. Same toy, only the look-again setting changed. That is a fair comparison, and it is still a toy. Leaves are not a toy, so I am only half sure what it means for them.
You ran the board once ({runs}). There is room for the other run whenever you like.
You ran the board {runTimes}, each time at the same setting ({runs}). That is a repeat, not a comparison yet. Change the one setting and it becomes one.
On the map, the lamps you saw yourself: {lamps}.
The ones you went back to ({kept}) were warm when you came in. That part is just true: a lamp warms when someone comes.
You saw it dip at {tide}. I drew a little wave there.
Someone hung a wish at {wish}. I did not read it. I watered the planter under it.
And the {gift}. It is on the windowsill by table 3.

close.keeper: Next: the shrine moss, and whether it stays green after a week with nobody on the steps. If it does, your reading has a problem, and I will tell you.
close.sink: Next: the shrine moss. If it curls after a week with nobody on the steps, I will tell you, even though I will hate it.
close.unsure: Next: the shrine moss, a week with nobody on the steps, one photo each evening. Then we will know a little more.
close.none: Next: the shrine moss. Come and look at it with me sometime.
